accuracy.evidence: Placement checked against DfE Development Matters (2021): Communication and Language, birth to three (enjoy singing, music and toys that make sounds) and Expressive Arts and Design, birth to three (move and dance to music; explore and respond to different sounds), with 3 and 4 year olds (play instruments with increasing control) as the next step; and Letters and Sounds (DfES 2007) Phase 1 Aspect 3 body percussion and Aspect 4 rhythm and rhyme. Beat (pulse) is defined as the steady tick under the song and kept distinct from the rhythm of the words, as in the Model Music Curriculum (DfE 2021) and Kodály practice. Lab timing checked: the Duke beat is a steady 650 ms (about 92 bpm, a walking march), elephant steps 800 ms halve to 400 ms mouse steps, the freeze pattern is 3 beats then 2 silent beats at 450 ms, and a tap counts if it lands within 45% of the gap (max 280 ms) of a beat, a forgiving window for 2 to 3 year olds. Parameterised answers n and n+1 are whole numbers 1 to 5 at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: tapping all the time instead of on the beat (off-beat taps turn the drum amber with 'Wait for the heart to light up'; predict 'Rain: pitter-patter, all mixed up'; m1, m4; challenge tag 'steady'), keeping the old speed when the beat changes (fast-part off-beat taps say 'Faster now! Quick little taps'; predict 'Stay slow'; p5; tag 'speed'), carrying on when the music stops (taps on the stop signs say 'Shh! The music stopped. Freeze!' and spoil the round; predict 'Keep tapping'; p1; tag 'stop') and clapping too many or too few or the wrong sound when copying (Teddy's count is repeated with 'Count with me: 1, 2, 3'; stomp for clap is refused; m7; tag 'count').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbeat runs a real beat clock and judges each tap against the time of the nearest beat, then changes tempo and inserts silent beats, so the child's timing is the mechanism. flagsyl (201 Syllables) claps the parts of single words with no tempo, flagsongrhyme (1042) is about rhyming word endings in songs, and flagbyheart (490 Songs and rhymes by heart) is about remembering lines; none times taps against a steady pulse, changes speed or has a freeze.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each idea by doing it: taps between hearts are not counted and the drum shows amber, taps on lit hearts earn stars, so the evenly spaced hearts show that the beat is steady; the elephant row of wide hearts turns into the mouse row at half the spacing and slow taps then miss, so the child speeds up; taps on the stop signs spoil the round, so the child learns to freeze; and Teddy's pattern must be matched in number and sound. Done messages state each idea after the scene has shown it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'Rain: pitter-patter, all mixed up' (the hearts light at the same gap every time and only taps near them count), 'Stay slow' (after four elephant beats, slow taps miss the quick mouse hearts) and 'Keep tapping' (tapping on the stop signs spoils the round).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating picture questions for child and grown-up; wrong options carry four tagged messages that each name the slip: stop (when the music stops, we stop too), count (copy the same number; count Teddy's claps), speed (big slow animals make a slow beat, small quick animals a fast one) and steady (a beat has the same gap every time, like a clock). In-scene feedback also names the slip, e.g. 'Teddy did 3. You did 2. One more!'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are four lines of two to five word sentences (Songs have a beat. Tick, tick, tick, like a clock.) within the family kid limit checked by validate_lessons.py; on the canvas there is one short banner line, emoji hearts, an emoji drum with 'Tap!', and star or 'of 2' counters, so a 2 year old can follow by picture while a grown-up reads. Terms such as pulse, rhythm and body percussion stay in the adult text, which passes the adult limit.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea (steady beat, ways to move with it, fast and slow, stop and freeze). Adult paragraphs give the EYFS and Phase 1 placement with key words, define beat versus rhythm, list four named mistakes with a caution about exact timing at this age, and say what each scene does. The content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the drum pad is about 220 by 96 px and centred under the hearts, the 8 march hearts fit one row with the Duke above the lit heart, the elephant and mouse hearts sit on two rows with the mouse hearts at half the spacing and no overlap, the 5 freeze discs fit one row, and the Clap and Stomp pads are about 100 px wide each; the young class makes the twin buttons large. Nothing is clipped; the iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Tap the drum' in the three beat scenes (keyboard presses are timed the same way as taps), Clap and Stomp for copying, and Tap, Clap, Stomp, Pat knees, Slow and Fast in free play. The canvas aria-label reports every hit, miss, freeze and copy result in words without announcing each beat, and sound stays optional (off by default) because every beat is also shown by a lit heart. axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
